content.value_statement: Replacing a Markdown renderer can break rendering, streaming, and HTML safety rules. This skill creates a migration plan that preserves behavior and documents remaining gaps.
actual_capabilities: Find Markdown renderer call sites and related plugin chains.
Classify migrations as direct, custom-renderer, plugin-heavy, or security-heavy.
Map custom renderer behavior to scoped Markstream component overrides.
Identify raw HTML, URL policy, and Mermaid settings that require review.
Recommend Markstream modes and smooth streaming settings for Vue 3.
Summarize direct mappings, open TODOs, and validation work.
limitations: It does not change code without a user request.
It cannot guarantee parity with unsupported parser plugins or transforms.
Trusted HTML and Mermaid policies still require application-specific security review.
It relies on available repository code and documentation.

use_cases.title: Replace a simple renderer
use_cases.description: Identify a low-risk renderer swap and preserve existing user-visible Markdown behavior.

use_cases.title: Migrate a customized chat UI
use_cases.description: Review custom renderers and streaming settings before moving an AI chat interface to Markstream.

use_cases.title: Assess complex Markdown pipelines
use_cases.description: Document plugin, sanitization, and HTML gaps before deciding whether a migration is appropriate.

prompt_templates.title: Find the current renderer
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this repository for its current Markdown renderer. List every call site and classify the migration risk.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a safe swap
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Markstream migration plan for the current Markdown renderer. Preserve styles and visible behavior first.

prompt_templates.title: Review custom rendering
prompt_templates.prompt: Map the custom Markdown renderers in this project to scoped Markstream component overrides. List any unsupported behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Assess streaming and security
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this chat Markdown migration for streaming, raw HTML, URL policy, and Mermaid risks. Recommend safe Markstream settings and validation steps.

output_examples.input: Audit a project that uses react-markdown with custom code blocks.
output: Review needed: custom code block rendering and raw HTML policy.

output_examples.input: Review a Vue 3 chat that streams Markdown content.
output: Use chat mode for the active chat row.
Keep smooth streaming enabled when only output pacing is needed.
Validate completed history with streaming disabled.

best_practices: Audit call sites and security settings before replacing the renderer.
Preserve current behavior before adding Markstream-specific features.
Run the smallest relevant test or build after each migration stage.
anti_patterns: Do not claim full parity before reviewing plugins and custom renderers.
Do not enable trusted HTML globally to match one legacy call site.
Do not move to nodes streaming when content streaming is sufficient.

faq.question: What does this skill audit?
faq.answer: It audits Markdown renderers, call sites, custom rendering, plugins, HTML handling, and streaming behavior.

faq.question: Does it migrate code automatically?
faq.answer: It provides a migration workflow and recommendations. Code changes require a separate user request.

faq.question: When is a migration direct?
faq.answer: A migration is direct when the application passes simple Markdown strings with little custom parser behavior.

faq.question: How does it handle custom renderers?
faq.answer: It maps tag-based rendering to scoped Markstream component overrides and records behavior that needs manual work.

faq.question: Does it review HTML safety?
faq.answer: Yes. It identifies raw HTML, URL policy, sanitization, and Mermaid settings that need application-specific review.

faq.question: When should nodes streaming be used?
faq.answer: Use nodes only for AST control, worker preparsing, or frequent structural updates. Use content streaming for simpler pacing.
